why_angle: The cited Schumacher and Advance Auto pages and the top roundups put a plug-in combo's 100–200 A engine start next to a pack's 1,000 A or more peak. None of them says these are different kinds of rating. This page explains the plug-in figure: it is a capped current from the wall, limited to 7 seconds per crank and under 3 seconds on a hard crank, with a 180 s cool-down after repeated cranks, and it needs a battery installed in the car. It then compares that with the pack combos that jump-start without an outlet.

page.title: Battery Charger with Jump Starter: Plug-In Engine Start vs Lithium Pack Combos
page.h1: Battery charger with jump starter: which combo does both jobs
page.desc: A plug-in charger's 100–200 A engine start boosts the car's battery from the wall, 7 s per crank. A Charge N Start pack jumps anywhere and still charges at home.
page.answer: Short answer. The Battery Tender Charge N Start 4120 is a 12V battery charger and jump starter combo: 4 A charging plus a 1,200 A pack that can jump start with no outlet. A plug-in charger's 100–200 A engine start is a capped wall current, 7 seconds per crank, not peak amps.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Recharge time. To put back half of a 50 Ah battery (25 Ah), best case before charging tapers: the Schumacher SC1281 or SC1353 at 6 A takes 25 ÷ 6 ≈ 4.2 h; the Charge N Start 4120 at 4 A takes 25 ÷ 4 ≈ 6.3 h; the Charge N Start 1100 or 1120 at 1 A takes 25 ÷ 1 = 25 h.
  • Waiting between starts. The Charge N Start needs 30 s between tries. A plug-in Schumacher forces a 180 s cool-down after repeated cranks: 180 ÷ 30 = 6 times the wait.
  • Charge N Start 1120 over the 1100. $149.95 − $139.95 = $10 for a 1,200 A pack instead of 1,000 A, rated for gas engines to 6.0 L and diesel to 4.0 L.
  • Wall draw during engine start. PlainPrepper lists the SC1281 at 20 A intermittent on 120 V: 20 × 120 = 2,400 W from the outlet while you crank.
Your situationFits
The car can die anywhere, and you also want a real charger at homeBattery Tender Charge N Start 4120
The car always sits within cord reach of a garage outlet, and you want the fastest rechargeSchumacher SC1281
A bigger engine, started in the garage, with a standard or AGM batterySchumacher SC1353 (200 A)
You want to jump anywhere, and the battery mostly needs maintaining, not recoveringCharge N Start 1120 or 1100 (1 A)
A 12 V lithium (LiFePO4) starting batterySchumacher SC1281L: Schumacher lists LiFePO4 support for it, while the SC1309/SC1353 manual allows lead-acid (standard or AGM) only

Engine-start amps are not peak amps

A plug-in charger with engine start does not carry its own battery. Schumacher's SC1281 manual says to connect it to a live grounded 120 V outlet. It also warns that using Engine Start without a battery installed in the vehicle could damage the vehicle's electrical system, because the charger adds its current to the car's own battery. Its 100 A is a capped rate fed from the wall. The manual limits each crank to 7 seconds and forces a 180-second cool-down after repeated cranking. It also says that if cranking draws more than the Engine Start Rate, crank time may be less than 3 seconds. Below 2 V or in extreme cold, it says to charge for 5 minutes before you crank. The SC1309/SC1353 manual adds 2 minutes of charging before the unit shows it is ready.

A combo with a lithium pack works the other way. Battery Tender says the Charge N Start's jump function runs from its internal cells whether or not the charger side is active, and on wall power the charger maintains both the car battery and the pack. Its 1,200 A is a peak figure from that pack, so 100 A against 1,200 A is not a 12-fold difference in starting power. A listing on Clamp & Crank shows how far peak can sit above usable current: the Stanley J7CS is rated 700 A peak and 350 A instant.

The capped 100 A can still start a big engine when the battery gets time to charge first. CarXplorer's Jordan Matthews started a drained 5.3 L V8 Silverado at 25 °F with the 100 A Schumacher SC1308 after a 2-minute 30 A boost. Schumacher lists the same 100 A start and 6 A charge for the SC1308L as for the SC1281L.
